g.text: Delivery — open-source CI, multi-account AWS, signed desktop releases
No long-lived AWS keys in CI. Infrastructure is CDK; the same artifacts move staging → production; desktop updates are signature-checked.
1 · Contributors open pull requests; CODEOWNERS and branch protection apply.
2 · CI runs lint, types, unit/property tests, golden vaults, security gates, license scan and SBOM, with pinned actions.
3 · On main, Actions federates by OIDC into a short-lived deploy role: no stored AWS keys.
4 · cdk deploy updates the staging account; acceptance and security tests run against it.
5 · After a manual approval the same assets deploy to production.
6 · Release tags build the desktop installers, which are signed and notarized with provenance.
7 · Installers and the signed update manifest go to the release bucket.
8 · CloudFront serves downloads and the update feed.
9 · The Tauri updater verifies the signature before installing anything.
10 · Every account logs to an organization CloudTrail in the log-archive account.
11 · GuardDuty, Config and Security Hub findings are aggregated in the security account.
